fields.sample_size: eight co-researchers (four postpartum mothers, four guardians; aged 20-43) from villages served by the Chimvu and Thekerani health facilities; about 281 photographs taken (140 + 141), 44 selected (21 + 23); gallery walks and group discussions
fields.study_design: qualitative participatory photovoice study with phenomenological analysis (NVivo 12) and community validation meetings
fields.effect_estimate: Photographs and narratives showed the physical toll of water collection, emotional stress, and heightened infection risk from inadequate sanitation among postpartum women; women are seldom included in community water discussions or formal governance structures where water decisions are made. Photovoice is presented as a tool for amplifying marginalised women's voices. Qualitative; no effect estimate.
fields.section: Full text: Abstract; Methods 2.2 (photovoice, sampling, validation with the communities); Results; Discussion

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a photovoice study with eight postpartum women or guardians in Thyolo District, Malawi found that water scarcity burdens postpartum health physically and emotionally and that women are excluded from community and formal water governance; qualitative, read in full text 2026-10-04.

notes: The first extraction had no sample; the full text gives eight co-researchers and the photo counts. Governance content is the exclusion of women from decision-making, reported by participants rather than tested.
